description: Named process scenarios. Each is a set of overrides on amcrax.schemas.CaseInputs defaults (the baseline). Process scenarios are solved in Aspen Plus V15 by aspen/automation/run_scenarios.py (results/simulations/<id>.json) and by the Python process model. Economic / environmental overlays (ammonia price, ammonia origin, heat source) are applied on top of any solved case by amcrax.scenarios and are not Aspen cases.

process_scenarios.label: Baseline (600 degC, 20 bar, heat-integrated)
process_scenarios.rationale: High-temperature operation typical of Ni-based catalysts; PSA-compatible pressure.

process_scenarios.label: Low-temperature cracking (500 degC)
process_scenarios.rationale: Temperature window associated with Ru-based catalysts; lower equilibrium conversion, lower sensible duty.

process_scenarios.label: High-temperature cracking (700 degC)
process_scenarios.rationale: Higher equilibrium conversion and lower ammonia slip at the cost of higher heat demand.

process_scenarios.label: Low-pressure cracking (5 bar)
process_scenarios.rationale: Thermodynamically favourable; the PSA would then need cracked-gas compression (not included in the Aspen flowsheet; evaluated in amcrax.separation).

process_scenarios.label: High-pressure cracking (40 bar)
process_scenarios.rationale: Delivers hydrogen at pressure from pumped liquid ammonia; equilibrium conversion penalty.

process_scenarios.label: No feed/effluent heat recovery
process_scenarios.rationale: Reference configuration to quantify the benefit of the feed/effluent exchanger.

process_scenarios.label: Tight heat recovery (20 K approach)
process_scenarios.rationale: Larger exchanger area in return for less trim heating.

process_scenarios.label: High PSA recovery (0.92)
process_scenarios.rationale: More product hydrogen, less tail-gas fuel: more imported heat.

process_scenarios.label: Low PSA recovery (0.75)
process_scenarios.rationale: More tail-gas fuel: approaches thermal self-sufficiency of the cracker.

process_scenarios.label: Fuel-cell-grade product (N2 slip 0.0005, recovery 0.80)
process_scenarios.rationale: The baseline product (392 ppm N2, 99.961 mol% H2) misses the 99.97 % / 300 ppm limits quoted for ISO 14687 fuel-cell hydrogen; a tighter N2 slip at a literature-typical recovery represents a purity-driven PSA operating point.

overlays.note: Overlay parameter values (prices, emission factors) live in backend/amcrax/data/economics.yaml and environmental.yaml with their sources.
